package_info.package_versions: 2023 version 18.3 and earlier; 2022 version 17.4.1 and earlier
package_info.why_malicious: Multiple critical vulnerabilities exist in the InDesign plugin responsible for parsing QuarkXPress Drawing (QXD) files. Attackers can exploit these flaws by delivering specially crafted QXD files that trigger improper memory access, resulting in memory leaks or arbitrary code execution. Simply opening a malicious QXD file can allow an attacker to execute code or exfiltrate sensitive information, posing a severe security risk.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a QXD file is opened and parsed by the InDesign plugin)
execution_context.file_location: InDesign plugin module responsible for decoding QuarkXPress Drawing (QXD) files
required_permissions: memory (to allocate and write to buffers)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: if (qxd_file.length > MAX_SIZE) { ... } // improper bounds check leading to out-of-bounds write
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (likely, as per Adobe plugin development)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a QXD file is opened, the code performs an insufficient bounds check on the file length, allowing attacker-controlled data to cause an out-of-bounds memory write, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code fails to enforce strict bounds checking on attacker-controlled file input, enabling out-of-bounds writes—a well-known vector for memory corruption and code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Proper file parsing routines must validate all input sizes and prevent writes outside allocated buffers; this code allows unchecked writes based on untrusted data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate plugins may parse complex file formats, but must always implement robust bounds checking to prevent memory corruption.
key_indicators: Improper or missing bounds check on file input size
Out-of-bounds memory write triggered by crafted QXD file
Memory corruption or crash upon opening malformed QXD files
Potential for attacker-controlled data to overwrite function pointers or control structures

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a QXD file is opened and parsed by the InDesign plugin)
execution_context.file_location: InDesign plugin module responsible for decoding QuarkXPress Drawing (QXD) files

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: data = qxd_file[offset]; // improper bounds check leading to out-of-bounds read
malicious_snippets.code_language: C++ (likely, as per Adobe plugin development)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a QXD file is opened, the code performs an insufficient bounds check on the file offset, allowing attacker-controlled data to cause an out-of-bounds memory read, resulting in leakage of sensitive information from process memory.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code allows reading outside the allocated buffer based on attacker-controlled offsets, which can expose sensitive memory contents to the attacker.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal file parsing must never permit reads beyond buffer boundaries; this behavior exposes internal memory and risks leaking secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate plugins may read file data, but must always enforce strict bounds checking to avoid exposing memory contents.
key_indicators: Improper or missing bounds check on file offset
Out-of-bounds memory read triggered by crafted QXD file
Potential leakage of sensitive process memory (e.g., credentials, internal data)
Crash or unexpected data exposure when opening malformed QXD files

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious QXD file with malformed data designed to exploit improper bounds checks in the InDesign plugin.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious QXD file is delivered to the victim, for example via email attachment, download link, or shared network drive.

attack_chain.action: Victim opens the malicious QXD file using Adobe InDesign, triggering the vulnerable plugin code.
attack_chain.leads_to: InDesign plugin processes the file, activating the vulnerabilities.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes: either arbitrary code execution via out-of-bounds write (snippet_1) or sensitive memory leakage via out-of-bounds read (snippet_2).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains code execution on the victim's system or access to leaked sensitive information from process memory.

behavioral_signatures: Opening QXD files in InDesign triggers memory access violations (e.g., access violation exceptions, crashes)
InDesign process attempts to execute code from memory regions associated with file input buffers
Unusual or excessive memory reads or writes during QXD file parsing operations
Unexpected process crashes or abnormal termination when handling QXD files
file_indicators: QXD files with malformed or oversized data sections (e.g., fields exceeding expected maximums)
QXD files that consistently cause crashes or exceptions in Adobe InDesign
QXD files containing anomalous or non-standard structure not conforming to QuarkXPress Drawing format
network_indicators: Not directly applicable unless attacker payload includes network exfiltration; monitor for suspicious outbound connections from the InDesign process immediately after opening QXD files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Adobe InDesign process crashes or access violation exceptions when opening QXD files, especially those involving memory corruption. Use endpoint protection or EDR solutions to detect exploitation attempts such as out-of-bounds memory access or code execution. Scan QXD files for malformed structures, oversized fields, or non-standard format deviations. Deploy IPS/EDR signatures for known exploit patterns targeting these vulnerabilities. If possible, monitor for unexpected outbound network connections from InDesign following QXD file opening, which may indicate successful exploitation and data exfiltration.
